domain_label: Study System — Explainability & Onboarding: Explainable-AI Explanation Interfaces (the honest 'why' surfaces)
purpose: How to turn the app's algorithmic decisions — the FSRS scheduler, the BKT/Elo learner model, the E1-E4 weakness diagnoser, the planExam feasibility planner — into honest, faithful, user-facing 'why' explanations (why this card now, why this weakness, why the plan changed), communicating uncertainty without false precision and, above all, never rendering a fixed heuristic constant (the Weakness 'confidence 80%') as if it were a computed probability.
assumptions: no observed dataset or usability study supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and every design-selection call is an ESTIMATE synthesized from the cited HCI/XAI literature and the app recon
the app today has ZERO tooltip/guide/explanation layer [FACT-source: APP_RECON §5.9], so every 'why' surface described here is greenfield, not a retrofit of an existing one

the tooltip-ladder UI mechanics, the guide page, and onboarding flow are the OTHER two KBs of this specialist; this KB owns only the EXPLANATION CONTENT — what a faithful, honest explanation of an algorithmic decision must contain and must never claim

XAI/HCI references (intelligibility question types, contrastive explanation, mental-model alignment, trust calibration) are carried as ESTIMATE — to source-verify because they were not source-verified in this build; all app-behavior facts trace to APP_RECON as cited
exclusions: the tooltip-ladder rendering mechanics (tiny caption -> hover card -> 'more' panel -> guide page) and the guide-page/onboarding information architecture — the sibling uxguide KBs own the UI delivery; this KB stops at the explanation's content and honesty contract

the internal math of the models being explained (FSRS-6 DSR, BKT posterior equations, Elo update, planExam interval ladder) beyond citing the exact fields and rules the explanation must faithfully reflect — those live in the sched, learner and sysloops specialists

actually building the missing scheduler/pipeline execution, closing the diagnosis->remediation loop, or persisting error_tags — this KB explains the app AS SHIPPED honestly, including explaining that certain advertised actions are text-only [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d]
visual-encoding, color and chart design (the viz specialist) beyond the requirement that a number's visual form not overstate its precision

competency_questions.question: What is the explanation problem for this app, and why does explainable-AI doctrine apply to a spaced-repetition scheduler and a weakness diagnoser at all?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: frames the goal as turning specialists' internal reasoning into honest user-facing 'why' surfaces for the scheduler/diagnoser/planner, notes the app has zero explanation layer today, and tags the XAI-selection as ESTIMATE

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names the why / why-not / what / what-if / how-to / inputs family, maps them onto the app's decisions, and marks the taxonomy ESTIMATE — to source-verify

competency_questions.question: Why must an explanation be FAITHFUL to the actual computation rather than merely plausible, and how does that shape the user's mental model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: distinguishes a faithful explanation (traces the real rule/fields that fired) from a plausible-but-fabricated one, ties an unfaithful explanation to a wrong mental model and miscalibrated trust

competency_questions.question: How does a 'why' surface trace a decision back to the exact rule and entity fields that produced it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: requires each explanation to cite the concrete fired rule / stored fields (e.g. the specific Weakness decision rule, the FSRS due date and retrievability) as its provenance, and forbids reasons not present in the computation

competency_questions.question: How do you honestly explain why THIS card is up for review right now?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: grounds the answer in the FSRS due date / retrievability and the new-card budget, and honestly notes the review queue is due-order only (mastery/Elo do NOT influence selection)

competency_questions.question: How do you explain why a weakness was diagnosed as E1-E4, and where the diagnosis actually comes from?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: maps E1-E4 to slip/misconception/missing_prereq/retrieval_decay, names the fired decision rule and its evidence, and states only the manual pipeline creates Weakness rows

competency_questions.question: How do you explain why the plan shrank or changed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: grounds plan changes in due-card counts, the new_per_day cap, the shared-minute budget share and the planExam feasibility verdict, and flags that planExam is a heuristic ladder, not an FSRS simulation

competency_questions.question: How must the Weakness 'confidence 80%' be presented so the user is not misled into reading it as a computed probability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the confidence is the hardcoded 0.4-0.8 constant of whichever rule fired (NOT a posterior), prescribes labeling it as a fixed heuristic tag, and forbids probability-bar visual forms that imply computation

competency_questions.question: How do you communicate uncertainty honestly and avoid false precision across all the app's numbers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: prescribes matching the displayed precision to the method's earned precision, distinguishing computed quantities from fixed constants, and using verbal hedges/ranges where a point number would overclaim

competency_questions.question: How do you disclose when displayed state is stale or its uncertainty is uncalibrated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: requires flagging state that depends on the never-scheduled pipeline (weaknesses, trend, calibration) and disclosing known-miscalibrated uncertainty (elo_theta_sd decaying to a floor regardless of outcome)

competency_questions.question: How do you explain why something did NOT happen, or that an action had no effect?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: supports why-not / contrastive questions and honestly explains no-op or text-only affordances (Mark Resolved only flips a status; missing_prereq 'blocking' is prose no code enforces)

competency_questions.question: What is the spec for an honest 'why' surface and the go/no-go verdict for the whole explanation layer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: composes provenance + right-depth + contrastive + honest-uncertainty into a surface spec, sets appropriate trust as the target, and issues a verdict: every explanation faithful, every number labeled computed-vs-heuristic, no false precision, absence and staleness disclosed

glossary.definition: The property that a user can obtain answers to questions about an automated decision — why it happened, why not something else, what the inputs were, what-if they changed. Framed as a set of question types an interface should support [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: Lim & Dey intelligibility-types line of HCI work].

A FAITHFUL explanation reflects the actual computation that produced the decision (the rule that fired, the stored fields it read); a PLAUSIBLE explanation merely sounds like a reasonable justification. XAI honesty requires faithfulness: a plausible-but-unfaithful explanation builds a wrong mental model and licenses misplaced trust.

The explanation surface answering 'why is this card up for review now'. Honest content: FSRS-6 next-due date and retrievability, plus the new-card budget — and the honest caveat that the review queue is strictly due-order, so BKT mastery and Elo difficulty do NOT influence which card appears [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d, §4b].

The explanation surface for a diagnosed Weakness. E1=slip, E2=misconception, E3=missing_prereq, E4=retrieval_decay (by enum order; the code never binds the letters). Honest content names the single decision rule that fired and its evidence, and states that only the manually-triggered pipeline ever creates these rows [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a].

The explanation surface for a shrinking or growing plan. Honest content: due-card counts, the new_per_day cap, the exam's prorated slice of the shared daily-minute budget, and the planExam go/tight/no_go feasibility verdict — flagged as a heuristic interval ladder, not an FSRS simulation [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3c, §4b, §6.12].

The single most load-bearing honesty rule of this KB: the Weakness 'confidence 80%' rendered by the UI is Math.round(w.confidence*100)% where w.confidence is the HARDCODED constant (0.4-0.8) of whichever diagnosis rule fired — it is NOT a computed posterior probability [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]. It must never be shown in a form that implies computation.

Displaying a number with more implied exactness than the method that produced it earns — e.g. a fixed constant as a probability, a heuristic percent to a decimal place, or a monotonically-decayed uncertainty shown as a live measurement. Avoiding it is a core requirement here (echoing the honesty tags the specialists carry internally).

A labeling scheme that separates numbers the system actually computed from data (FSRS retrievability, BKT posterior, calibration Brier/logloss) from fixed rule constants and static configuration (rule confidence, the 0.10 slip / 0.30 guess caps, format weights), so a user (and a tooltip author) can tell which is which.

The goal that an explanation produce APPROPRIATE trust — neither over-trust of a confident-looking UI sitting on a heuristic, nor under-trust that makes the user ignore a genuinely computed signal. Honest uncertainty disclosure is the lever; a polished number over a constant is the classic over-trust trap [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: automation-trust/reliance HCI literature].

An explanation that accounts for something NOT happening or an action having no downstream effect: why a concept was not flagged, and honestly that 'Mark Resolved' only flips a status field (no scheduling change) and that missing_prereq 'block new cards' is advisory prose no code enforces [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d, §4a].

nodes.definition: Frame the job: the app makes algorithmic decisions the user cannot see into — an FSRS-6 scheduler picks what is due, a per-concept BKT/Elo learner model estimates mastery, a rule-based diagnoser emits E1-E4 weaknesses, and a heuristic planExam issues feasibility verdicts — and today it explains NONE of them: there is zero tooltip or guide layer [FACT-source: APP_RECON §5.9]. Explainable-AI doctrine (explanation interfaces for algorithmic decisions) is the right lens because each of these IS an algorithmic decision a user will ask 'why' about. The task of this KB is to turn the specialists' internal reasoning into honest, faithful user-facing 'why' surfaces — why this card now, why this weakness, why the plan shrank — without overclaiming what the underlying computation actually knows [ESTIMATE, high confidence — XAI framing is standard; the per-app selection is design judgment].

included: the scheduler/learner-model/diagnoser/planner as the algorithmic decisions needing explanation
the zero-explanation-layer starting point
the turn-internal-reasoning-into-honest-why-surfaces mandate
excluded: the tooltip-ladder UI mechanics and guide page (sibling KBs)
the internal math of the models being explained

pros.claim: Naming the app's four algorithmic decisions as explanation targets scopes the 'why' work to real, high-value surfaces instead of decorating everything
pros.example: committing to why-this-card, why-this-weakness and why-the-plan-changed as the three anchor surfaces

cons.claim: Deciding which decisions deserve an explanation surface is a design judgment made before any usability data exists
cons.example: assuming users most want the weakness explanation when they might actually want the scheduler explained first

failure_modes: treating explanation as cosmetic tooltips rather than faithful accounts of real decisions
explaining decisions the app does not actually make while leaving the real ones opaque

nodes.definition: Enumerate the intelligibility question types an explanation surface can answer and map them to the app: WHY (why did this happen), WHY-NOT (why not the alternative), WHAT (what is this number/state), WHAT-IF (how would changing an input change the output), HOW-TO (how do I get outcome X), and INPUTS/OUTPUTS (what does the decision read and produce) [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: Lim & Dey intelligibility-types HCI work]. For this app the dominant needs are WHAT ('what is FK6 Pathology mastery', 'what is confidence 80%'), WHY ('why this card', 'why this weakness'), and WHY-NOT ('why isn't concept X flagged'); WHAT-IF ('what if I raise desired_retention') is valuable at the planner. Choosing which types each surface supports keeps the explanation scoped and prevents promising a what-if the app cannot actually simulate.

included: the why/why-not/what/what-if/how-to/inputs question-type family
the mapping of those types onto the app's surfaces
picking which types each surface commits to answering
excluded: the wording/plain-language rendering of each answer (technical-communication, sibling KB)
the tooltip depth mechanics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: source-verifying the taxonomy or an unmet question type changes the type map

pros.claim: A question-type checklist makes an explanation surface's coverage explicit and catches unanswered user questions early
pros.example: noticing the weakness surface answers WHY but has no WHY-NOT for 'why wasn't my other concept flagged'

cons.claim: The taxonomy is a synthesized HCI frame, not verified here, and over-applying it can bloat a surface with question types users never ask
cons.example: adding a what-if simulator to a simple 'what is this number' caption nobody needed

failure_modes: promising a what-if the app cannot actually compute
supporting only WHY and leaving WHAT and WHY-NOT unanswered
acceptance_tests: the question-type family is listed, mapped to concrete app surfaces, and marked ESTIMATE — to source-verify
revisit_triggers: the taxonomy is source-verified or replaced

nodes.definition: Establish the non-negotiable rule of XAI honesty: an explanation must be FAITHFUL — it must reflect the computation that actually produced the decision (the rule that fired, the stored fields it read) — not merely PLAUSIBLE, a reasonable-sounding story invented after the fact [ESTIMATE, high confidence — faithfulness-vs-plausibility is a core XAI distinction; to source-verify against the interpretability literature]. A plausible-but-unfaithful explanation is worse than none: it reads as authoritative while teaching a wrong model of how the app works. Concretely, a 'why this card' tooltip must derive from the FSRS due computation, and a 'why this weakness' tooltip from the exact fired diagnosis rule; it may never fabricate a reason (e.g. 'because your mastery dropped') that the code did not use.

included: the faithful-vs-plausible distinction as a hard honesty rule
the requirement that every explanation derive from the real computation
the ban on plausible-but-fabricated reasons
excluded: the mechanism for pulling the real computation into the UI (provenance node)
the depth/wording of the faithful explanation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unfaithful explanation found in the wild or a computation change tightens the rule

pros.claim: Requiring faithfulness makes an explanation auditable against the code and blocks confident fabrication
pros.example: rejecting a 'why this card' string that cites mastery when the queue is provably due-order only

cons.claim: A strictly faithful explanation can be less satisfying or harder to phrase than a smooth plausible one, tempting authors to embellish
cons.example: the honest 'it is simply the oldest-due card' feeling thinner than an invented adaptive-sounding reason

failure_modes: shipping a plausible narrative that the computation does not support
explaining a decision by a factor the code never reads
acceptance_tests: the node states faithfulness as a hard rule, requires each explanation to trace the real computation, and forbids fabricated reasons even when plausible
revisit_triggers: an explanation is found citing a factor the code does not use

nodes.definition: State the purpose an explanation serves: it should build a CORRECT mental model of how the app works, so the user's expectations match the system's behavior [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: Kulesza/Norman mental-model line of HCI work]. An explanation is judged not by how satisfying it feels but by whether the model it induces predicts the system correctly. This has two honesty consequences: (1) an unfaithful explanation seeds a wrong model that will be violated later (the user expects adaptivity the queue does not provide); (2) an explanation should proactively correct a likely-wrong prior — e.g. users assume 'confidence 80%' is a probability, so the surface must actively dispel that, not merely avoid reinforcing it.

included: the correct-mental-model goal as the evaluation criterion for an explanation
the two honesty consequences (no wrong-model seeding; actively correct likely-wrong priors)
excluded: the specific likely-wrong priors per surface (handled where each surface is defined)
trust-calibration mechanics (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a mental-model study or a discovered misconception changes the alignment targets

pros.claim: Judging explanations by the mental model they induce gives a concrete success test beyond 'sounds clear'
pros.example: testing whether a user, after reading the tooltip, correctly predicts that mastery does not change which card is next

cons.claim: Mental models are hard to measure without user studies, so this criterion is aspirational until tested
cons.example: asserting a tooltip builds the right model with no study to confirm the user actually predicts behavior correctly

failure_modes: seeding a wrong model that later behavior violates
leaving a common misconception (confidence = probability) uncorrected because the copy merely avoids the word
acceptance_tests: the node makes correct-mental-model the evaluation criterion and derives both honesty consequences (no wrong-model seeding; proactively correct likely-wrong priors)
revisit_triggers: a usability study measures the induced mental model
a systematic user misconception is discovered
system behavior changes such that old models mislead

nodes.definition: Define the mechanism that makes faithfulness operational: every 'why' surface must carry PROVENANCE — a pointer to the exact rule that fired and the concrete entity fields it read. For a weakness, that is the specific decision rule (e.g. 'same misconception_tag chosen >=2x -> misconception, confidence 0.8') and the ItemOption.misconception_tag / prereq mastery it consumed [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]. For a card, the FSRS due date, retrievability_at_review and the new-card budget [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3a, §4b]. For a plan, the due counts, new_per_day cap and budget share [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3c]. The explanation text is generated FROM this provenance, so it cannot drift from the computation; a surface with no traceable provenance is not shipped.

included: provenance as a pointer to the fired rule and the fields it read
generating explanation text from provenance so it cannot drift
the no-provenance-no-ship rule
excluded: the per-surface content of card/weakness/plan explanations (their own nodes)
how deep the provenance is disclosed to the user (depth ladder)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rule/field change or a divergence finding tightens the provenance requirement

pros.claim: Anchoring every explanation to a fired rule and named fields makes it auditable and self-updating when the code changes
pros.example: regenerating the weakness tooltip from the rule id so a rule change automatically updates the copy

cons.claim: Wiring provenance out of backend functions into the UI is real engineering the app has not done, so this is greenfield instrumentation
cons.example: needing the pipeline to emit which rule fired and its evidence, which it does not currently expose to the client

failure_modes: writing explanation copy by hand that silently diverges from the rule it claims to describe
shipping a surface whose stated reason has no traceable provenance
acceptance_tests: the node requires each surface to point at the fired rule and read fields, generates text from that provenance, and refuses to ship a surface without traceable provenance
revisit_triggers: a decision rule or field is renamed/changed
a new decision surface is added without provenance wiring
an explanation is found diverging from its cited provenance

nodes.definition: Author the honest 'why is this card up now' surface. Faithful content: the FSRS-6 scheduler set this card's next-due date from its stability/difficulty and the desired_retention workload dial, and the review queue serves the first due cards in due order, mixing new (capped by new_per_day, though the queue does not actually enforce that cap) and review cards [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3a, §3d, §4b, §6.7]. The critical honesty caveat: BKT mastery and Elo item difficulty do NOT influence which card appears — the learner model is display-only, so the surface must NOT imply the card was 'adaptively chosen for your weakness' [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d]. The explanation reads the card's own CardState due/retrievability as provenance.

included: FSRS due/retrievability and the new-card budget as the honest reason
the due-order queue behavior and the unenforced new_per_day caveat
the explicit no-adaptivity honesty caveat
excluded: the FSRS-6 math itself (sched specialist)
changing the queue to be adaptive (out of scope)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an adaptive queue or new_per_day enforcement changes the honest reason

pros.claim: A faithful card explanation grounded in FSRS due order stops the UI from implying adaptivity it does not have
pros.example: 'due today because FSRS scheduled it for ~90% recall' instead of 'chosen because you are weak here'

cons.claim: The honest answer ('it is just due') is less flattering than an adaptive-sounding one, and admits the mastery model is not driving selection
cons.example: a user disappointed that their diagnosed weakness does not change what they see next

failure_modes: implying the card was adaptively selected for a weakness when the queue is due-order only
citing the new_per_day cap as enforced when the review queue ignores it
acceptance_tests: the surface grounds the reason in FSRS due/retrievability and the new-card budget and explicitly states mastery/Elo do not drive selection

nodes.definition: Author the 'why was this diagnosed as a weakness' surface for the E1-E4 differential. E1=slip, E2=misconception, E3=missing_prereq, E4=retrieval_decay (enum order; the code never binds the letters explicitly) [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]. Faithful content names the single rule that fired and its evidence: a repeated misconception_tag (>=2x) -> misconception; a prereq concept below 0.5 mastery -> missing_prereq; a low-retrievability miss with mastery>=0.5 -> retrieval_decay; a single miss at mastery>=0.6 -> slip; else the under-sampled fallback ('probe with 2-3 varied items') [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]. Two honesty musts: state that only the manually-triggered pipeline creates these rows (so they can be stale), and never present the attached confidence as a computed probability (handed to the confidence node).

included: the E1-E4 -> slip/misconception/missing_prereq/retrieval_decay mapping
naming the fired rule and its evidence as the reason
the manual-pipeline-origin and confidence-is-not-a-probability honesty flags
excluded: the honest rendering of the confidence number itself (its own node)
the diagnosis math/thresholds' validity (learner/sysloops specialists)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rule/threshold change or scheduled pipeline execution updates the surface

pros.claim: Explaining the exact rule and evidence turns an opaque 'E2 misconception, 80%' badge into an auditable account the user can act on
pros.example: 'flagged because you picked the same wrong option (tag: reversible_pulpitis) twice'

cons.claim: Exposing the rule reveals how coarse the heuristic is (single-miss slip, fixed thresholds), which can undermine confidence in the diagnosis
cons.example: a user seeing that 'slip' fired on exactly one miss and doubting the whole diagnosis layer

failure_modes: presenting the diagnosis as adaptive/learned rather than a fixed rule cascade
omitting that only the manual pipeline creates and refreshes these rows
acceptance_tests: the surface maps E1-E4 correctly, names the fired rule and its evidence, and flags both the manual-pipeline origin and that confidence is not a probability
revisit_triggers: the diagnosis rules or thresholds change

nodes.definition: Author the 'why did the plan change' surface. Faithful content: tomorrow's planned_units comes from counting CardState due by tomorrow and capping new cards at Settings.new_per_day [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3b stage 4]; the Planner's per-exam 'New/day', 'Budget share' and feasibility go/tight/no_go come from planExam splitting a shared daily-minute budget pro-rata by card count and binary-searching the max sustainable new/day within it [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3c, §4b]. Two honesty musts: flag that planExam is a heuristic interval ladder (x2.3 with clamped retention scaling), NOT an FSRS simulation, so its verdicts inherit that approximation [FACT-source: APP_RECON §6.12]; and that a plan can silently shrink from a 500-row query cap truncating due counts at scale [FACT-source: APP_RECON §6.3]. So 'the plan shrank' may mean fewer due cards, a lower budget share, OR a silent truncation.

included: due-count + new_per_day cap + budget-share + feasibility verdict as the honest reasons
the planExam-is-a-heuristic-not-FSRS caveat
the silent-truncation-at-scale caveat
excluded: fixing the truncation or replacing the heuristic ladder (extint/sched specialists)
the planExam math internals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an FSRS-simulated planner or raised query caps change the honest reasons

pros.claim: Decomposing a plan change into due-count, budget-share and feasibility makes an alarming 'plan shrank' legible and non-scary
pros.example: 'fewer cards today because 30 fewer are due, not because you fell behind'

cons.claim: Honestly surfacing the heuristic-not-FSRS and silent-truncation caveats exposes real system limitations the user might rather not see

nodes.definition: Adopt contrastive explanation as the natural shape of a 'why' answer: people ask 'why THIS rather than THAT', so the strongest explanations state the contrast case, not just the cause [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: Miller's contrastive-explanation synthesis in the XAI literature]. In this app: 'why this card and not that one' -> because its FSRS due date is earlier; 'why misconception and not slip' -> because the same wrong tag was chosen twice, which the slip rule (single miss) does not match; 'why was concept A flagged and not B' -> because A's evidence tripped a rule and B's did not. Contrastive framing sharpens the explanation and directly answers the WHY-NOT intelligibility type, but it requires the provenance of BOTH the chosen and the foil outcome.

included: contrastive why-this-not-that as the answer shape
concrete app contrasts for card/weakness selection
the requirement to have the foil's provenance too
excluded: the full why-not/no-op absence handling (its own node)
the wording of the contrast

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: foil provenance availability or source verification changes the contrastive scope

pros.claim: Contrastive framing answers the question users actually ask and makes a diagnosis rule's boundary visible
pros.example: 'misconception not slip because the same wrong answer repeated — slip needs a lone miss'

cons.claim: Producing a faithful contrast needs the foil outcome's provenance, which the app may not compute (it does not enumerate why B was not flagged)
cons.example: being unable to say why concept B escaped diagnosis because the pipeline only records positives

failure_modes: inventing a contrast the computation cannot support
giving a bare cause where the user needed a this-not-that contrast
acceptance_tests: the node frames answers contrastively, gives concrete app contrasts, and requires the foil's provenance before asserting a contrast
revisit_triggers: the app starts recording negative/foil provenance

nodes.definition: Define the CONTENT at each depth of a 'why' answer (distinct from the sibling KB's tooltip UI mechanics): layer 1 a one-line honest reason ('due today for ~90% recall'); layer 2 the contributing factors and the honest caveats ('queue is due-order; mastery does not affect it'); layer 3 the full rule/formula and provenance ('rule: same misconception_tag >=2x; confidence is a fixed 0.8 constant'). The rule: each deeper layer ADDS faithful detail and never CONTRADICTS a shallower one, and no layer omits a caveat load-bearing enough to mislead if the user stops there [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: progressive-disclosure HCI principle]. Depth trades comprehensibility against completeness; the honesty constraint is that the shallow layer must not be true-but-misleading on its own.

included: the one-line / factors+caveats / full-rule content layering
the add-detail-never-contradict rule
the no-load-bearing-caveat-omitted-at-shallow-depth constraint
excluded: the tooltip-ladder rendering (tiny caption -> hover -> panel -> guide) UI mechanics (sibling KB)
the guide page structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a misleading shallow layer or a sibling-KB layer change updates the depth rule

pros.claim: Layering content by depth lets a novice get a true one-liner and an expert drill to the rule without either being lied to
pros.example: 'due today' at layer 1 expanding to the FSRS retrievability and due-order caveat at layer 2

cons.claim: A short honest layer risks omitting a caveat that makes it misleading alone, so choosing what the one-liner may drop is delicate
cons.example: '80% confidence' at layer 1 without the 'fixed constant' caveat reading as a probability

failure_modes: a shallow layer that is technically true but misleading without its caveat
a deeper layer that contradicts rather than refines the shallower one
acceptance_tests: the node specifies the three content depths, requires deeper layers to add-not-contradict, and forbids omitting a load-bearing caveat at the shallowest depth
revisit_triggers: a shallow layer is found misleading in isolation
the sibling tooltip-mechanics KB changes the number of layers

nodes.definition: Set the doctrine for communicating uncertainty honestly: match the displayed precision to the precision the method actually earns, and prefer a verbal hedge or a range to a false point estimate when the underlying quantity is soft [ESTIMATE — to source-verify: uncertainty-visualization / risk-communication HCI work]. nodes.definition: The load-bearing honesty node. nodes.definition: Require disclosure when a displayed uncertainty is known to be miscalibrated. The clearest case: elo_theta_sd (and elo_b_sd) decay monotonically toward a 0.3 floor no matter how surprising outcomes are, so the model's stated uncertainty becomes systematically overconfident over time [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d]. Any surface that leans on this uncertainty (a probe trigger, a 'we are confident' framing) must either not present it as a live confidence or must disclose that it is a decayed lower bound, not a measured spread. More broadly, where the app measures calibration (CalibrationBin Brier/logloss) but never feeds it back to correct desired_retention or the FSRS weights [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d], an explanation must not imply the system self-corrects when it does not.

nodes.definition: Require an explanation to disclose when what it shows may be STALE. The structural fact: nothing is scheduled — the 'nightly' pipeline runs only when the user presses the Dashboard button, so Weaknesses, MasteryHistory (the trend chart), CalibrationBin, SystemMetrics and tomorrow's plan all drift until that click [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3b, §3d, §6.1]. A 'why this weakness' or mastery-trend surface must therefore carry provenance of WHEN it was last computed and flag staleness, rather than presenting stale diagnosis as current truth. Related honest limits: the trend chart needs >=2 distinct run dates to render at all, and re-running the pipeline on the same day wipes a same-day 'resolved' mark [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d, §4a]. Freshness is itself part of a faithful explanation.

nodes.definition: Handle the honesty-critical case of explaining what did NOT happen or an action with no effect. edge_cases.description: A depth layer collapses to the full formula for a novice, overwhelming rather than informing
edge_cases.trigger: the deepest provenance is shown by default with no one-line entry point
edge_cases.mitigation: lead with a true one-liner and gate the full rule/formula behind an explicit deeper layer

edge_cases.description: A why-not question ('why isn't concept X flagged') is answered with a confidently wrong reason
edge_cases.trigger: the app records only positives, so no foil provenance exists, yet a reason is asserted
edge_cases.mitigation: honestly state 'no rule fired for it, or it has not been analyzed yet' rather than inventing a cause

edge_cases.description: A feasibility 'go' verdict is explained as an exact FSRS-simulated guarantee
edge_cases.trigger: the planExam heuristic ladder result is surfaced without its approximation caveat
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the verdict as a heuristic estimate that can diverge from real FSRS load, not a guarantee

workflow.action: Frame the app's algorithmic decisions as the explanation targets
workflow.description: Identify the scheduler, learner model, diagnoser and planner as the decisions needing honest 'why' surfaces, from a zero-explanation baseline
workflow.gate: the four decisions and the zero-layer baseline are named with sources and the per-app selection tagged ESTIMATE

workflow.action: Map intelligibility question types and set the faithfulness rule
workflow.description: List why/why-not/what/what-if types per surface and require every explanation to be faithful to the computation, not plausible
workflow.gate: each surface's supported question types are listed and the faithful-over-plausible rule is stated as non-negotiable

workflow.action: Instrument decision provenance for each surface
workflow.description: Wire each surface to the fired rule and read fields so its copy is generated from provenance and cannot drift
workflow.gate: every anchor surface points at a fired rule and named fields; none ships without traceable provenance

workflow.description: Explain due-now from FSRS due/retrievability and the new-card budget with the no-adaptivity caveat
workflow.gate: the reason is grounded in FSRS due/retrievability and states mastery/Elo do not drive selection

workflow.description: Explain E1-E4 by naming the fired rule and evidence, flag manual-pipeline origin and non-probability confidence
workflow.gate: E1-E4 mapped, fired rule and evidence named, manual-origin and confidence-not-a-probability flagged

workflow.description: Explain plan changes from due counts, new_per_day cap, budget share and feasibility, with heuristic and truncation caveats
workflow.gate: plan changes grounded in due/budget/feasibility and both the heuristic-not-FSRS and silent-truncation caveats present

workflow.action: Set the honest-uncertainty and computed-vs-fixed rules
workflow.description: Match precision to method, tag every number computed or fixed, and make the confidence constant read as a preset
workflow.gate: each surfaced number is tagged computed/fixed, precision matches method, and the confidence constant is not a probability

workflow.action: Add calibration, staleness and absence disclosures
workflow.description: Disclose the elo_sd decay, flag pipeline-dependent staleness with last-computed time, and explain no-ops/text-only affordances
workflow.gate: elo_sd decay disclosed, stale state flagged, and Mark-Resolved/prereq-blocking stated as advisory/no-op

workflow.action: Translate honesty tags and target appropriate trust
workflow.description: Render internal FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags as plain hedges and calibrate presentation to each signal's underpinning
workflow.gate: no raw tags in copy, and presentation confidence matches the strength of the underpinning

workflow.action: Compose the honest-surface spec and issue the verdict
workflow.description: Assemble the six-clause surface spec and issue the GO (three anchor surfaces) / NO-GO (no constant-as-probability, no fabrication, no stale-as-current)
workflow.gate: the six-clause spec and the GO/NO-GO with its acceptance rule are stated with sources

priority_rationale: The problem frame, intelligibility types, faithfulness rule and mental-model goal come first because they decide that every 'why' surface must be a faithful account of the real computation aimed at a correct mental model; decision provenance and the three anchor surfaces (why-this-card, why-this-weakness, why-the-plan-changed) come next as the concrete faithful explanations grounded in the app's actual rules and fields; the uncertainty stack (honest uncertainty communication, the confidence-is-a-constant rule, false-precision avoidance, computed-vs-fixed tagging, calibration and staleness disclosure, explanation of absence) then supplies the honesty machinery that keeps those surfaces from overclaiming; and trust calibration, honesty-tag surfacing, the composed honest-surface spec and the go/no-go verdict come last because they compose every upstream rule into a single auditable standard with an explicit refusal to render a fixed heuristic constant as a computed probability.

dominance_rules.rule: Faithfulness dominates engagement in any explanation
dominance_rules.rationale: a plausible-but-unfaithful explanation reads as authoritative while teaching a wrong model of the app
dominance_rules.trigger: engaging copy would state a reason the computation does not use
dominance_rules.action: ship the faithful account and make it engaging only through wording and depth, never through fabrication

dominance_rules.rule: A fixed heuristic constant never appears as a computed probability
dominance_rules.rationale: the Weakness confidence is the fired rule's hardcoded 0.4-0.8 constant, not a posterior [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]
dominance_rules.trigger: the confidence (or any constant) is about to be rendered as a percent/probability bar
dominance_rules.action: render it as a preset label distinct from computed calibration numbers

dominance_rules.rule: Displayed precision is capped at the precision the method earns
dominance_rules.rationale: spurious decimals and continuous gauges on heuristic or stepped values manufacture certainty the method lacks
dominance_rules.trigger: a noisy, fixed or stepped value is about to be shown with decimals or a measurement-style visual
dominance_rules.action: round to an approximate band or a preset label and drop the measurement visual

dominance_rules.rule: Staleness disclosure dominates a clean current-looking presentation
dominance_rules.rationale: pipeline-dependent state drifts until the manual run and stale diagnosis shown as current misleads
dominance_rules.action: attach a last-computed timestamp and flag possible staleness with a refresh prompt

dominance_rules.rule: Honest no-op disclosure dominates preserving an affordance's appeal
dominance_rules.rationale: presenting a status-flip or advisory prose as an effective action gives the user a false sense of progress
dominance_rules.trigger: Mark Resolved, prereq-blocking, or probe affordances are explained
dominance_rules.action: state exactly what the action does and mark text-only affordances advisory, not enforced

dominance_rules.rule: Plain-language translation dominates raw honesty-tag jargon
dominance_rules.rationale: exposing FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN verbatim is faithful but unintelligible, violating the mental-model goal
dominance_rules.trigger: an internal honesty tag is about to reach user copy
dominance_rules.action: translate it into a plain hedge that preserves its epistemic weight

dominance_rules.rule: A one-line honest layer dominates a default full-formula dump
dominance_rules.rationale: leading with the deepest provenance overwhelms and buries the reason for a novice
dominance_rules.trigger: a surface would show the full rule/formula by default
dominance_rules.action: lead with a true one-liner and gate the full provenance behind a deeper layer

dominance_rules.rule: An honest single cause dominates an invented contrast when the foil has no provenance
dominance_rules.rationale: the app records only positives, so asserting why-not without foil provenance fabricates a reason
dominance_rules.trigger: a why-not question lacks computed foil provenance
dominance_rules.action: give the honest available cause and decline the foil rather than invent one

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosed miscalibration dominates a clean confidence figure
dominance_rules.rationale: elo_theta_sd decays monotonically to a floor regardless of outcome, so its 'confidence' is structurally overconfident [FACT-source: APP_RECON §3d]
dominance_rules.trigger: an elo_sd-derived uncertainty is about to be shown as a live measurement
dominance_rules.action: disclose it as a decayed lower bound or do not present it as live confidence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish provenance for a surface before writing any of its explanation copy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hand-written copy that silently diverges from the rule it claims to describe and must be rewritten

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every surfaced number computed-vs-fixed before choosing its visual form
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a probability bar for a fixed constant and having to redesign it once its nature is noticed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the faithful reason and its load-bearing caveats before drafting the one-liner
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a shallow layer that reads true-but-misleading and has to be re-scoped after review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm an affordance's actual effect before writing its explanation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: describing a no-op or advisory prescription as an enforced action and reworking it when the code is checked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach a last-computed timestamp to pipeline-dependent surfaces from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retrofitting staleness disclosure across every diagnosis/trend surface later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the plain-language translation of each honesty tag before templating copy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: raw FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN jargon leaking into shipped tooltips and a mass find-replace

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check whether foil provenance exists before promising a contrastive answer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a why-not surface the app cannot honestly populate and tearing it out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compose the six-clause honest-surface spec before mass-authoring surfaces
anti_rework_rules.prevents: surfaces that each miss a different honesty clause and need per-surface honesty patches

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real scheduler is added so the pipeline runs automatically
iteration_protocol.action: relax the staleness disclosures on pipeline-dependent surfaces and re-check the last-computed provenance

iteration_protocol.trigger: the diagnoser is changed to emit a real posterior probability instead of a fixed constant
iteration_protocol.action: re-author the confidence presentation from preset-label to a genuinely-computed probability with earned precision

iteration_protocol.trigger: the review queue becomes adaptive (mastery/Elo wired into selection)
iteration_protocol.action: update the why-this-card reason to reflect adaptive selection and drop the no-adaptivity caveat

iteration_protocol.trigger: elo_theta_sd is changed to update on surprise rather than decay to a floor
iteration_protocol.action: revise the calibration disclosure and allow the uncertainty to be shown as a live measurement

iteration_protocol.trigger: remediation enforcement or probe scheduling is implemented
iteration_protocol.action: re-label the prereq-blocking and probe affordances from advisory to active in the absence explanations

iteration_protocol.trigger: a usability study measures the mental model or trust a surface induces
iteration_protocol.action: adjust depth, wording and hedges to close the gap between induced and warranted trust

iteration_protocol.trigger: an XAI/HCI reference carried as ESTIMATE is source-verified or corrected
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade or revise the affected nodes' claims and tags accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new algorithmic decision surface is added to the app
iteration_protocol.action: run it through the six-clause honest-surface spec and add its provenance and caveats

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run

evaluation_suite.regression_policy: re-run evaluation suite after any node addition or formula change
